notes: The only human named is the scribe Nārāyaṇaśarman (śarman is a brahmin name-suffix rather than an office title; the 〇 is a string-hole mark in the transliteration). The three phrases gopālagati (!), śrīvaidyanāthagati (!), rāmacandragati (!) follow the devotional verse 'matir bhavatu govinde' and read most naturally as devotional formulas ('Gopāla/Vaidyanātha/Rāmacandra is [my] refuge', gati for gatiḥ, hence the cataloguer's (!)) naming the deities Gopāla (Kṛṣṇa), Vaidyanātha (Śiva) and Rāmacandra; they are therefore not listed as persons. They could conceivably be later ownership/reading notes by persons bearing those names, but nothing supports this. 'hariharābhyāṃ namaḥ' is a salutation to deities. Visapīgrāma is unidentified (Mithila region presumed). Catalogue fields agree with the colophon; LS 507 ≈ 1626 CE.
